messages:
harper: Quick design sync: I'm iterating on the SLO slider + guardrail presets for autoscale. Need copy + accessibility feedback before tomorrow's design review.
mika: Love the presets but the labels feel vague. Current: Aggressive / Balanced / Safe. Suggest: Low-latency, Balanced, Cost-saving. More explicit.
owen: Agreed. Also the slider currently says 'Target latency' 9	can we change to 'SLO latency (p99) - ms'? Make units visible.
harper: Good call. I'll update label to 'SLO latency (p99) — ms'. What about helper copy under presets? Right now it's long.
tess: Keep each preset to one short fragment: 'Low-latency: best performance, higher cost', 'Balanced: cost & latency tradeoff', 'Cost-saving: lower cost, higher latency'. Add a tooltip with details.
mika: Accessibility: the preset chips must be a real radio group with legend for screen readers. Also include aria-describedby on the slider that references the 'why this matters' text.
harper: Noted. For visual design, I'm worried that three presets + slider + guardrails looks busy on small screens. Maybe collapse presets into an accordion labeled 'Quick presets'.
owen: If we hide them behind accordion, new users might not discover them. Alternative: show compact chips by default, reveal full descriptions on hover/focus.
tess: Copy nit: guardrail toast messages after applying a preset are currently passive. Make them actionable: 'Preset applied. View settings' with a link back to the slider. 
ops-bot: Reminder: when showing units, use ms integer formatting. Also ensure the slider step matches SLO granularity (50ms steps for p99).
harper: OK I'll: (1) rename presets to explicit labels, (2) set slider label to SLO latency (p99) - ms, (3) use radio group markup, (4) shorten microcopy and add tooltip, (5) make presets visible as compact chips that expand on hover/focus. Will post updated frames and a small PR today. :thumbsup:
